Subject: ClearLake discovery recap — PII, retention & support access (next steps)

Hi Sara / JD —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the concrete asks I captured so we can align next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of requirements you shared:
- PII scope: patient identifiers + billing metadata (name, DOB, MRN, billing IDs). Some payloads will be tokenized/hashed post-ingest; raw identifiers are required for billing and reconciliation.
- Data residency: production data must remain in US regions only (primary in us-east-1) with no cross-border backups.
- Retention: regulatory requirement to retain certain records for 7 years; others may be pruned at 1 year.
- Logging & audit: need immutable audit logs for access to PII (who, when, reason) retained for 3+ years and available to your SOC for spot checks.
- Support access: prefer JIT (just-in-time) scoped access for support engineers with RBAC and short TTLs. Break-glass for emergencies must be logged and require a two-person approval.

Attachments Im including: redwood-data-handling-matrix.xlsx (matrix tying data classes -> residency/retention/logging), SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf (what we can share), and a sample MA template.

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) Well draft a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) covering specific residency, retention windows, and support access workflow — target for your review by Mon, Jul 19.
2) Technical deep-dive with your infra/security + our security/infra team to walk through KMS, key ownership options, and network isolation (30–45m). Proposed slots: Tue Jul 20 or Wed Jul 21.
3) Vivek will propose an RBAC model (SCIM group mapping + least-privilege roles) and a break-glass runbook we can simulate.

Are there any additional compliance docs your procurement/security team needs up front? JD — looping you in for procurement concerns.

Thanks,

—

Hi Dylan —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- PII scope: for most clinical workflows we can hold de-identified tokens, but as noted billing needs the full identifiers. Well flag which buckets require RAW storage (billing/audit).
- Retention: 7 years for billing and legal hold; other analytics data can be retained 12 months. We will provide a retention matrix.
- KMS: preference is for customer-managed keys (CMK) in our AWS account if possible. We need clarity on whether Redwood can operate with a CMK + cross-account decrypt for operational tasks.
- Break-glass: we require a documented approval flow and post-event forensic timeline. Also asking whether access can be restricted to named individuals (not broad support groups) during break-glass events.

JD (procurement) — please note: well need to include data residency language in the MSA and a specific SLA for audit log retention.

Karen — Im copying our external consultant so she can advise on the CMK/forensics ask.

Happy to take the MAP and provide comments. Thanks —

Sara
VP Product Operations
ClearLake Health

Subject: Re: ClearLake discovery recap — proposed technical controls

Adding a short technical proposal we can surface in the follow-up deep-dive. Ill turn these into a one-pager and attach a JIT playbook draft.

1) RBAC & provisioning
- Use SCIM provisioning from ClearLake IdP into role-scoped groups in Redwood (billing-readonly, billing-admin, support-jit).
- Enforce least-privilege by default; billing admin role limited to a small named group (approx 3 individuals).

2) Support access / JIT
- Support engineers request ephemeral access via our support portal tied to a ticket id. Access grants TTL=30m by default, with justifications required.
- Break-glass path: emergency access request -> 2nd approver (on-call security) + automated Slack/escalation notification -> access logged + session recording where applicable.

3) KMS / key management
- Support CMK where ClearLake owns the key; Redwood can support cross-account decrypt patterns (limited ops) but needs an agreed playbook for key rotation and emergency decrypt.

4) Logging & retention
- Immutable, append-only audit logs pushed to your SIEM via secure forwarder (retention policy configurable; we recommend 3y for audit logs).
- Access logs include requestor, roles, justification, session id, and tokenized correlation id for traceability.

Action items from here:
- Monica: prepare a short RBAC role map and SCIM mapping example (attached: support-jit-playbook.md).
- Dylan: send MAP draft to Sara & JD by Mon 19 Jul.
- Marissa: confirm what we can redact in shared SOC2 artifacts and prepare a redacted pack.

Happy to present these on the technical deep-dive. Vivek

--
